# Appeal — denied for no prior authorization

**Use when:** service was performed and denied for missing auth. Strongest when the
procedure was urgent/medically necessary, or when a screening converted to diagnostic
intra-operatively (common in GI — you cannot pre-authorize a polypectomy you don't yet
know is needed).

**Deadline:** most commercial appeals are 180 days from the denial date. Check the EOB.

Claim #: [CLAIM NUMBER] · Denial date: [DATE]

To Whom It May Concern:

We appeal the denial of the above claim for lack of prior authorization.

**Grounds:** [select]
1. **Intra-operative conversion.** The procedure was scheduled and authorized as a
   screening [colonoscopy/EGD]. During the procedure [findings — e.g. a polyp was
   identified and removed], converting it to a therapeutic service. The need could not
   be known in advance and could not have been separately authorized. Operative and
   pathology reports enclosed.
2. **Medical urgency.** The service met the plan's urgent/emergent exception at
   [CITE PLAN PROVISION]. Delaying for authorization would have posed risk to the
   patient. Clinical documentation enclosed.
3. **Authorization was on file.** Auth [NUMBER] was issued [DATE] for [CODES]. Copy
   enclosed; the claim appears to have been processed without it being matched.
4. **Eligibility verified.** Coverage was verified on [DATE] and no authorization
   requirement was disclosed. Reference [CALL REF / 271 transaction] enclosed.

**Requested action:** overturn the denial and process $[AMOUNT] for payment.

Enclosed: EOB · operative report · pathology report · [auth / 271 / call log].

Respectfully,
[NAME], [TITLE] · [PHONE] · [EMAIL]
